summary.headline: GHCL Textiles Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR446 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 20.6%, with management guiding Q3 margins between Q1 and Q2 levels.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR446 crores (up 31% YoY, up 9% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR92 crores (up 141% YoY) at a 20.6% margin versus 11.2% a year earlier. Adjusted PAT was INR56 crores after excluding a one-time INR27 crore exceptional loss from a fire at a rented Tuticorin warehouse; reported PAT was INR36 crores. Cotton prices rose sharply late in the quarter, prompting buyers to restrict purchases to immediate needs, and management expects Q3 spreads and margins to fall between Q1 and Q2 levels. Management reiterated the INR2,500 crore revenue and 15–18% EBITDA margin goal for FY30 and announced a new INR410 crore spindle and rooftop solar project.

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.2% a year earlier; Q1 was about 17%
+223% YoY; reported PAT INR75 crores, +155% YoY
Net debt-to-equity 0.03x; about INR74 crores debt repaid in H1

financial_highlights.value: About INR27 crores pre-tax (about INR20 crores post-tax)
financial_highlights.change: Inventory lost in August 2026 fire at rented Tuticorin warehouse; insured, claim in progress

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Fabric share of revenue rose to about 16% (16.5% per later remark) from 11% a year earlier; management targets 16.5–17% by year end. Meenakshi unit has reached full capacity.

segments.name: Yarn / spinning
segments.commentary: Operating at about 99% capacity utilisation. Spread was INR160/kg in Q1 and INR173/kg in Q2; October was similar to September and November is expected to be slightly lower.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 8% of Q2 revenue; about 30–35% of exports go to Bangladesh.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 spreads and EBITDA margin expected between Q1 and Q2 levels (Q3 closer to Q1; Q4 closer to Q2), with Q4 supported by seasonal demand and 11 MW solar and knitting benefits.
FY28 revenue of about INR1,800 crores considered very likely by management, after an analyst extrapolated H1 run-rate; management said this was not formal guidance.
Long-term goal of INR2,500 crores revenue at 15–18% EBITDA margin by FY30 reiterated.
Management said Q1 and Q2 margins are largely sustainable given vertical integration, green power, product mix and FTA tailwinds, though higher raw material prices will take time to absorb.
Management does not currently plan a share buyback; capital will go into growth.
capex_capacity: Of INR1,035 crores committed under the Tamil Nadu MoU, INR675 crores has been invested; the balance (about INR360–400 crores) is under discussion with the state government for incentive eligibility, with a capital subsidy of about INR145 crores mentioned by an analyst.

New INR410 crore board-approved project (includes working capital margin money) for 58,368 spindles and 5 MW rooftop solar; expected revenue INR400–420 crores at 14–15% EBITDA margin. Completion by end FY28, full benefit in FY29.
Knitting expansion: all 40 machines to be in place by Q3 FY27, with benefits from Q4 FY27. Incremental knitting capex about INR7–8 crores.
11 MW ground solar expected to be commissioned by end Q3 (December 2026), taking total green energy to 76 MW; capex about INR32 crores.

PM MITRA Park: 56 acres allotted; processing unit capex of INR275–300 crores, expected commissioning around FY30 due to SIPCOT common infrastructure delays. Total land bank about 250 acres; surplus land book value about INR100 crores.
demand_pricing: Domestic cotton rose from about INR64,000/candy to INR69,000/candy during the quarter and has been around INR67,000 since, now at parity with global cotton.
Buyers limited purchases to immediate needs when cotton and yarn prices spiked late in Q2; management said domestic demand remains steady with strong order flow.
Government removed import duty on cotton, extended to December 2026; management says imported inventory build in the next three months will be limited.
UK and New Zealand FTAs are in force (benefits expected in about a year); India-EU agreement expected to be operational in early 2027; Oman FTA also mentioned.
Lower cotton inventory provided a gain that management described as not sizable. Working capital rise was mainly cotton advances, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further expansions beyond 58,000 spindles, and when will projects come on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Spindle project benefits expected full year FY29; PM MITRA processing unit around FY30; 11 MW solar in December 2026; 40 knitting machines by Q3 with results from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread rose from INR160/kg in Q1 to INR173/kg in Q2; Q3 expected between these levels. Demand described as robust across exports and domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What were the drivers of margin expansion and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited: higher fabric share, lower power costs from green energy, product optimisation with strategic customers, market tailwinds and some benefit from lower cotton inventory. Management believes Q1–Q2 margins are largely sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: How much was spent on the fire and is it insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Entire inventory was insured; investigation by police and forensics to conclude by Q3 end, with recovery expected by year end after deductible. Fire was at a rented godown away from factory premises; no prior such incident at factory.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,850 crore FY28 revenue figure guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not guidance but agreed that about INR1,800 crores in FY28 looks highly likely based on H1 run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PM MITRA Park delayed and is there a garmenting plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay due to SIPCOT common infrastructure tenders and DPR redrafting; cushion built into timelines. Garmenting is being looked at favourably with nothing to announce; PM MITRA Park is settled and garmenting would be additional.

risks_watch: Cotton price volatility: buyers have curbed purchases and spreads may compress in Q3 as cotton costs pass through.
Insurance claim (about INR27 crore inventory loss) recovery timing and deductibles; investigation expected to conclude by Q3 end.
PM MITRA Park timeline has slipped to around FY30 and capex may rise above INR300 crores; Tamil Nadu incentive eligibility for the INR410 crore project is still under discussion.
Peak realisations: an analyst flagged the risk that FY28 growth depends on new capacity, as current utilisation is about 99%.
Bangladesh LDC extension and FTA benefit timing (a year out) affect export volumes; exports are only about 8% of revenue.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident on Q2 results and demand, but repeatedly flagged near-term margin pressure from rising cotton prices. It deflected on exact FY28 revenue and garmenting timelines and gave no firm guidance.
key_quotes: Overall, we delivered a robust Q2.
So overall, I think somewhere between Q1 and Q2 is where our yearly margin would be.
Marshal Sonavane: Resham ji, no plan as of now. Our focus is more on growth side, right?
we are looking at it favorably. I have nothing to announce right now, but yes, we are looking at it favorably.

adds.what: 58,368 spindles (new INR410 crore board-approved project, incl. 5 MW rooftop solar)
11 MW ground solar (green energy to 76 MW)
PM MITRA Park processing unit (56 acres allotted)

growth.why: Management guides Q3 EBITDA margin between Q1 (17%) and Q2 (20.6%) levels and FY28 revenue of about INR1,800 crores (analyst extrapolation, not formal guidance), backed by 99% utilisation, a new INR410 crore spindle project completing by end FY28, and 11 MW solar and knitting additions due in Q3/Q4 FY27, but cotton-price pressure and buyer restraint temper near-term outlook.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides Q3 EBITDA margin between Q1 (about 17%) and Q2 (20.6%) levels, closer to Q1, so margins hold near the high teens but compress from Q2 as cotton costs pass through; Q4 is guided closer to Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 11 MW ground solar is due by December 2026 (total green energy to 76 MW), 40 knitting machines are in place by Q3 with benefits from Q4, and the INR410 crore spindle project (58,368 spindles) is board-approved for completion by end FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Yarn utilisation is at about 99% and fabric share is rising toward 16.5–17% by year end from 11% a year earlier, with management describing domestic demand as steady and order flow strong.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A INR410 crore board-approved spindle and rooftop solar project was announced with 99% utilisation, and a further PM MITRA processing unit of INR275–300 crore is planned for around FY30.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called FY28 revenue of about INR1,800 crores very likely (analyst extrapolation of H1 run-rate, not formal guidance), but Q3 margin is guided down from Q2 levels.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cotton rose from about INR64,000 to INR69,000 per candy, buyers curbed purchases, and management expects Q3 margin to fall between Q1 and Q2 levels; spread was INR173/kg in Q2 and should compress toward Q1's INR160/kg.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Garmenting is being looked at favourably with nothing announced, and would be additional to the settled PM MITRA Park project.

rows.label: Tamil Nadu incentive eligibility for INR410 crore project and MoU balance
rows.why: INR675 crore of INR1,035 crore MoU is invested; the balance of about INR360–400 crore is under discussion for incentives, with a capital subsidy of about INR145 crore mentioned by an analyst.

rows.label: Insurance recovery on Tuticorin warehouse fire
rows.when: by end Q3 to year end
rows.why: About INR27 crore pre-tax inventory loss is insured; investigation concludes by Q3 end and recovery is expected by year end after deductible, which could add a one-time inflow.

rows.label: Cotton import duty removal extended to December 2026
rows.why: Duty removal is extended to December 2026, but management says imported inventory build will be limited over the next three months, so cotton cost relief is capped.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 results, demand and sustainability of Q1–Q2 margins, but cautious on cotton-driven Q3 margin pressure and deflected on FY28 revenue and garmenting timelines; analysts pushed on FY28 growth depending on new capacity with utilisation at 99%.
